text:
emily: quick checkin on admission proxy handshake design. goal: avoid double-admits when edges and central race under heavy churn.

rahul: we saw this in staging yesterday. two edges accepted provisional tokens and central reconciler later tripped oversubscribe.

dez: suggestion: edge does optimistic admit but attaches provisional_id and ttl; central keeps a tiny provisional ledger and confirms by exchanging provisional_id -> final_token. edges revoke if not confirmed in ttl.

emily: how small is tiny? need to keep contention low but tolerable with network jitter.

rahul: propose ledger window 300ms for edges close to central; provisional budget capped per-tenant to avoid large oversubscribe. if central unreachable edges fallback conservative (halve provisional allotment).

dez: also recommend a fast invalidation channel: central publishes short invalidation msgs to edges via pubsub so they can clamp local counters before reconciliation completes. ensures quicker stop of abusive spikes.

ops-bot: experiment result: https://ci.company/perm/proxy-handshake/try-3 9% oversubscribe reduction, 2% added reconciliation traffic.

emily: UX: responses include header X-Redwood-Provisional: id=abc123;ttl=300ms and later X-Redwood-Confirm: id=abc123 when central confirms. apps can surface this for debugging.

rahul: testing: multi-edge replay, cold central, and cross-region latency spikes. also simulate flaky pubsub to ensure safe defaults.

dez: i'll draft PR with proto messages and a tiny simulator. aiming to post in 48h.

emily: thanks, will add to rollout checklist and schedule a short canary window once PR lands.
